plan: Produce immutable candidate004 from candidate003 with identical arithmetic in all three kernels (forward elementwise weighted SwiGLU, input_grad two-halves store, wgrad native 2D [XBLOCK=1,RBLOCK=next_pow2(H)] FP32 accumulate then tl.sum(axis=1)[:,None]) and identical launch params (fwd/bwd BLOCK=1024 num_warps=4; wgrad XBLOCK=1 RBLOCK=next_power_of_2(H) num_warps=8 when RBLOCK>=2048 else 4 num_stages=1). Only the dispatch/caching changes; the frozen stage34 contract, gates, tolerances, native/control, seeds, timing and promotion rule are untouched.

Root cause confirmed in the vendor JIT launcher source: the compile/launch key ends with (..., use_sme, shape_info) and get_corex_sme returns empty shape_info for these pure elementwise/reduction kernels, so the launcher appends every tensor's actual .shape to shape_info. Candidate003 keys its own cache by exact (numel,N,grid), so each new expert token count is a fresh miss that re-enters kernel[grid](...), hits a fresh vendor shape_info key, and JIT-recompiles (220 compiles / 268 launcher_body in the untimed cProfile). do_not_specialize cannot remove shape_info; only bypassing the launcher on reuse does.

Fix: cache the IMMUTABLE CompiledKernel object (the bin returned by kernel[grid](...)) rather than a fixed-grid runner. First call for a key is a miss: kernel[grid](args, constexprs..., num_warps, num_stages, enable_sme=False) compiles once (going through the vendor launcher) and launches; store the returned bin. Every later call with the same key is a HIT: recompute the CURRENT grid (gx=ceil(numel/BLOCK) for fwd/bwd, (N,1,1) for wgrad) and launch via bin[(gx,1,1)](current runtime tensors + runtime numel/N), which runs CompiledKernel.c_wrapper directly, never recomputing the vendor key and never touching shape_info/JIT.

Make one bin valid across all N by marking the runtime size args do_not_specialize via supported string names (verified constructor normalizes str->regular_args.index): fwd/bwd kernels @triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["numel"]) and wgrad @triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["xnumel"]). This drops both the divisible-by-16 and the equal_to_1 specialization on those args, so a bin compiled at any token count (including a single-token N==1 expert, where xnumel would otherwise fold to constexpr 1) stays correct for every other count. H/TWO_H/XBLOCK/RBLOCK stay constexpr; numel/N stay regular runtime args still passed to the kernel.

Cache key reuses one bin only within an identical compiled-binary class and never forces shape-specific recompiles: key = (phase, device, dtype, H, BLOCK-or-RBLOCK, num_warps[, num_stages/XBLOCK], and every pointer data_ptr()%16). Pointers are NOT do_not_specialize, so their divisible-by-16 class is baked into the bin; including each pointer's %16 in the key guarantees we never reuse an aligned-compiled bin for an unaligned (offset-view) pointer. No exact numel/N/grid appears in the key because the arithmetic no longer needs it. For the contract (H=2048 fixed, fresh aligned allocations) this collapses to ~3 distinct keys / ~3 vendor compiles instead of one per expert count.

Pass enable_sme=False on every compile (miss) call: it is a documented vendor launcher kwarg (default True in the generated signature) and avoids compiler SME shape-dependent optimization for these pure elementwise/reduction kernels that contain no dot/GEMM. It does NOT remove the shape_info key (the bin-reuse bypass does that); at hit time enable_sme is irrelevant because bin[grid](...) skips the launcher entirely.

Keep a guarded reuse path with _state['closure_ok']: if bin[grid](...) ever raises on a hit (vendor runner rejecting the runtime args), flip closure_ok False, clear the cache, and from then on always take the correct plain kernel[grid](...) JIT path. This is a bin-reuse-unsupported guard only; there is NO hidden whole-operator fallback to native on supported shapes. The public entry weighted_swiglu keeps the exact candidate003 guard predicate (CUDA, BF16/BF16, x.dim() in (2,3), weights.dim()==2 last-dim-1, both contiguous, even last dim, weights.shape[0]==flattened rows) and delegates the whole call once to native only for genuinely unsupported inputs (CPU/FP32/non-contiguous/shape mismatch).

Preserve all boundary behavior: forward allocates a fresh (prefix,H) BF16 out and only launches when out.numel()!=0 (empty N0 skips kernels); backward does g=g.contiguous(), fresh dx=empty_like(x)/dw=empty_like(weights), launches input_grad then wgrad with N=numel//H only when g.numel()!=0. The wgrad loop uses rmask=rindex<H so tail widths H=257/769 mask correctly; masked other=0.0 keeps empty/odd widths safe within unchanged atol 3e-4/rtol 1e-3. Nothing cached is ever an output/input tensor, full pointer, or stream; the bin fetches the active stream per launch like native. Imports limited to torch, triton, triton.language; no env/file/network/seed/feedback/native-cache access and no hardcoded observed values.

Validation order is unchanged and not pre-judged: candidate004 must independently pass the 44-case probe + 2 actual offset views + 48 actual-native replays (bitwise) + the 3-step full-training comparisons (2627 checks / 1289 tensors) BEFORE any performance claim, then fresh full-MoE numerical admission, then the formal 9-process/120-step three-arm timing across seeds 34102/34103/34104 with first 20 discarded. Cross-shape bin reuse must pass those numerical gates with zero native fallbacks first. Compile counters will be checked in a separate untimed run; no speed/throughput gain is claimed until measured.
risks: The bin-reuse bypass (bin[(gx,1,1)](current args)) relies on vendor Triton 2.4.1 CompiledKernel.__getitem__ producing a runner that launches c_wrapper with current tensors, runtime numel/N and the live stream. Candidate003's equivalent runner-call path passed all 48 replays with zero fallbacks, so this is low-risk, but if a future vendor build changes the runner arity, closure_ok flips and every launch degrades to the correct-but-slower JIT path, so the >1% gain gate may not be met even though numerics are unaffected.

do_not_specialize must actually drop both divisible-by-16 and equal_to_1 for numel/xnumel in this vendor so a single bin is valid for N==1 through N==256; the constructor/launcher source shows specializations skip do_not_specialize indices and configs.equal_to_1 is derived from the same specialization, which supports this, but if the vendor still specialized xnumel==1 separately the single-token expert would need its own key (still correct, just an extra compile).

Pointer %16 is included in the key, but torch CUDA allocations are typically >=256-aligned so most keys collapse to %16==0; the 2 offset-view probes may land in a different alignment class and trigger one extra compile each. This cannot harm correctness, only cache-hit density.

Bitwise parity still depends on the vendor compiler lowering the copied [XBLOCK=1,RBLOCK] accumulate + tl.sum(axis=1)[:,None] to the identical FP32 reduction association as the original Inductor triton_red_fused_mul_silu_sum_1; this is inherited unchanged from candidate003 (which passed), but the bin is now reused across shapes, so if any shape-dependent codegen difference existed it would surface at the numerical gate.

enable_sme=False is passed only on the compile/miss call; if a vendor path ignored it and still emitted an SME shape-dependent binary, reusing that bin across N could in principle differ, though these kernels have no dot/GEMM/SME-eligible ops so the SME branch should be inert.

int32 offset arithmetic (TWO_H*x0 up to ~2.1M for N=256,H=2048) is safe for the declared moe-weighted contract shapes but would overflow for much larger inputs; candidate004 targets only the observed contract.

If a harness pins a stream around the module hook, the bin runner's per-launch stream fetch must be re-confirmed by the two fresh-input non-default-stream probes; no tolerance, timing, dtype or baseline-fusion weakening is introduced to compensate.
